summary: Frontend-only P0 bug-fix verification for 'Manufacture the book' one-click action on /projects. Logged in as Founder, opened /projects (projects-page rendered). Confirmed gold 'Manufacture the Book' button (data-testid project-render-<pid>) is visible alongside 'Open workflow' (data-testid project-open-<pid>) for the in-progress BOOK project 55e1992d… ('Introduction to forex trading', stage 'Manuscript & Chapters'). Regression: verified render buttons are NOT emitted for any of the video/podcast/audiobook projects currently in_progress (checked 0a5373ad… and 78b22130… — both are video/in_progress with no render button, as expected). Clicked Manufacture: 'Manufacturing your product…' toast appeared immediately; ~52s later the success toast 'Product manufactured — your downloadable file is ready.' fired. Items drawer auto-opened (data-testid project-items-<pid>) and listed 5 deliverables (data-testid project-deliverable-<pid>-0..4) — Readable Edition (HTML), High-Res Poster (PNG), Book Readable Edition (HTML), Digital eBook (EPUB), Print-Ready PDF. Every href points to https://…/api/rendering/asset/… (verified /api/rendering/asset/ substring). PDF and EPUB both present. Stage pipeline advanced past Manuscript, Cover & Interior Design, Quality Review → current stage now 'Founder Approval' (needs_approval); recommended-next-action text (data-testid project-next-<pid>) reads 'Your approval is required at “Founder Approval”. Approve to continue automatically.' — explicitly mentions approval as required. URL stayed on /projects (did NOT bounce to Cover Studio / flagship-showcase). The Approve & continue button (data-testid project-approve-<pid>) now renders because status is needs_approval. All 6 requested testcases pass end-to-end.
critical_code_review_comments: ProjectsContinuity.js renderProduct() opens the PDF via window.open in a background tab — expected per the request note. Since the drawer already shows the download links, this second-tab open can be a bit surprising on slow connections; consider making it opt-in or scrolling to the deliverables instead. Non-blocking.

GET /factory-os/projects/{pid}/items appears to return deliverables aggregated across the entire linked KR — the book project's items drawer also lists two 'Poster' deliverables (HTML + PNG) that were manufactured earlier from the same KR when a poster project ran. This does not break the spec (PDF/EPUB for the Book are present) but may confuse the Founder about which deliverables belong to which product. Consider filtering /items by project_id or product_type.
The BACKEND fallback in ProjectsContinuity.js line 10 (`|| ''`) is fine but a hard fail-fast (raise if missing) would surface misconfigured envs earlier — non-blocking.

renderProduct catches any error into a toast but does not restore itemsOpen state on failure (drawer will remain closed since we reset items[pid]=undefined before the /items GET). If the render call fails the user sees only the error toast, which is acceptable but a small polish opportunity.

rca of the issue: Root cause of the original founder complaint ('clicking Go bounces me to Cover Studio and I can never render'): the /projects page only offered an 'Open workflow' shortcut which routed users into the stage-specific studio (Cover Studio for design stage, Product Manufacturing for manuscript stage, etc.), where actual rendering was locked behind gates the Founder was not expected to complete manually. Fix (implemented and verified): ProjectsContinuity.js now renders a gold 'Manufacture the {outcome_name}' button next to 'Open workflow' for non-video/non-podcast/non-audiobook outcomes when the current stage is in_progress. The button calls POST /api/factory-os/projects/{pid}/render which (per continuity.py render_product) resolves the verified KR, generates the product via the LLM, calls deliverable_renderer.ensure_deliverable to materialise PDF/EPUB/HTML files, marks every workflow stage complete and advances the project to the 'Founder Approval' gate. The UI then auto-opens the items drawer, refreshes the deliverables list (all served under /api/rendering/asset/) and opens the primary PDF in a new tab. Verified: no redirect to Cover Studio, stage now 'Founder Approval', downloadable files present.
